decision.explanation: Since (7-4x)^2 ≥ 0, the left side 3(7-4x)^2+5 is at least 5 and cannot be less than -25. Therefore there is no solution.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the quadratic term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(7-4x)^{2}+5 & <-25 \\ 3(7-4x)^{2} & <-30 \\ (7-4x)^{2} & <-10\end{aligned}
$$

However, $(7-4x)^{2}\ge 0$ for all values of $x$ because the power $(2)$ is even.

Therefore, there is no solution to the given inequality.

Question 3
?

Solve the inequality 2(x−2)6−1≥3.

a
x≤2−26
b
−4−26≤x≤−4+26
c
x≤−26 or x≥26
d
x≥26
e
x≤2−26 or x≥2+26
Submit

decision.explanation: Adding 1 and dividing by 2 gives (x-2)^6 ≥ 2. Thus |x-2| ≥ the sixth root of 2, so x ≤ 2-\sqrt[6]{2} or x ≥ 2+\sqrt[6]{2}.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-2)^{6}-1 & \ge 3 \\ 2(x-2)^{6} & \ge 4 \\ (x-2)^{6} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{(x-2)^{6}} & \ge \sqrt[6]{2} \\ |x-2| & \ge \sqrt[6]{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-2\le -\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x-2\ge \sqrt[6]{2}
$$

So, the solution is

$$
x\le 2-\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x\ge 2+\sqrt[6]{2}.
$$

Solve the inequality 2(x−2)6−1≥3.

a
x≤2−26
b
−4−26≤x≤−4+26

x≤−26 or x≥26

Correct
EXPLANATION

Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find 2(x−2)6−1≥32(x−2)6≥4(x−2)6≥2.

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get (x−2)66≥26|x−2|≥26.

This corresponds to the following compound inequality: x−2≤−26orx−2≥26

So, the solution is x≤2−26orx≥2+26.

content.worked_solution:
Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-2)^{6}-1 & \ge 3 \\ 2(x-2)^{6} & \ge 4 \\ (x-2)^{6} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{(x-2)^{6}} & \ge \sqrt[6]{2} \\ |x-2| & \ge \sqrt[6]{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-2\le -\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x-2\ge \sqrt[6]{2}
$$

So, the solution is

$$
x\le 2-\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x\ge 2+\sqrt[6]{2}.
$$
